profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.address: 21721 Filigree Court, Suite A, Ashburn, VA 20147
profile.reading: This building is Equinix's DC6 facility on Equinix's Ashburn, Virginia campus, part of what Data Center Dynamics has called the birthplace of the commercial internet: AOL built the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support dial-up internet operations, and the fiber infrastructure that project attracted helped trigger the region's growth into Data Center Alley in Loudoun County, now described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet. Equinix established its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and DC2, which followed, has been described by Data Center Dynamics as reputedly the most connected building on earth; Equinix's own published specifications for DC2 describe a single-story, reinforced-concrete, 118,446-square-foot facility with N+1 power redundancy, a minimum cabinet density of 4kVA, 120v/208v power distribution, generators rated for 30 hours or more at full load, N+1 cooling redundancy, a 99.9999%-plus global guaranteed uptime commitment, and certifications including HIPAA, ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and NIST 800-53/FISMA High. Equinix has continued expanding the Ashburn campus well beyond DC1 and DC2, eventually building out numbered facilities into the twenties as demand grew, with Data Center Frontier reporting on Equinix's plans for a fleet of four-story buildings as part of that expansion. Equinix positions the Ashburn campus as serving one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast, offering colocation in private cages, smart-hands support, managed solutions, internet exchange access, metro connectivity, cross-connects, and its own Equinix Fabric and Fabric Cloud Router interconnection products. Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code but, consistent with the rest of Equinix's public site, does not publish this specific building's power capacity or square footage beyond the DC2 example cited above as representative of the campus's general specifications.

reading.body:
Equinix DC6 in Ashburn is a 59,374 square foot facility with no published power capacity. It sits within Equinix's 15-facility Washington DC metro campus, the largest single metro region in the operator's portfolio, positioned as North America's largest peering point and a major gateway to Europe. The broader Ashburn corridor, which extends into Culpeper County, has emerged as a sustained expansion zone for this critical infrastructure hub.

No power capacity is published for this building on its operator page, so its scale in megawatts cannot be assessed. Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, but only 23 publish power figures. This facility's contribution to the state's 1,375.4 MW of published capacity is therefore unknown, placing it outside the top 23 disclosed capacity sites.

Without published power figures, the number of AI accelerators or training racks this building can house cannot be calculated. Its relevance to AI scaling depends on unpublished specifications. The facility's value likely derives from its position within Equinix's metro peering and interconnection network rather than from IT load capacity alone, but neither the local technical specification nor the role it plays in the campus's overall configuration is disclosed.
